name_reason: Compliant with global naming: data_fd2_<domain=audio>_<descriptor>. Descriptor reflects both purpose (per-chapter player-turn BGM track ids) and data type (per-chapter array/table of byte track ids). No Ghidra address residue in the name. The '30' dimension is carried by the type (byte[30]); chapter count is a domain dimension, not address noise.
purpose: Read-only per-chapter lookup table giving the FDMUS BGM track id to play during the player's turn; indexed by current_chapter_id (0 = chapter 1 .. 29 = chapter 30).
logic_summary: 30-entry const byte array. Accessor everywhere is MOVZX EAX, byte ptr [chapter_id + 0x51E63] (unsigned, stride 1); the resulting track id is passed to fd2_set_bgm_track_with_fade. Read at four sites: fd2_run_full_turn_cycle (sets player-turn BGM in the new-player-turn phase, and twice compares this table vs the enemy-turn table @ 0x51E81 to decide whether to fade BGM out between phases), fd2_main_menu_continue_dispatcher (NEW GAME, CONTINUE committed-slot, and fallback engine-reload paths), fd2_load_save_and_init_engine (full engine reload from FD2.SAV), and main (NEW-GAME re-entry after a chapter event). No writers.
element_semantics: Each element is an 8-bit FDMUS BGM track id for the player's turn in that chapter; element index i corresponds to chapter (i+1). Observed values: {0x03,0x04,0x08,0x13}.
comment_original_issue: Per-symbol block was accurate but listed only two of the four readers (omitted main @ 0x25E47 and fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @ 0x10473) and did not state the exact accessor/stride.
notes: Memory at 0x51E63 (30 bytes) byte-identical to the src initializer. All 8 xrefs are READ/DATA (no writers), confirming const. Verified accessor opcodes directly at xref sites 0x25E47 and 0x10473 (both MOVZX byte ptr [chapter_id + 0x51E63]) and the comparison-then-fade logic in fd2_run_full_turn_cycle. Ghidra plate was empty (null) -> created concise plate consistent with src. Ghidra .gpr modified (plate metadata only; FD2.LE binary unchanged); program saved after commit.
